sights.address: Old Main, Pollock Rd, University Park, PA 16802
sights.w: The symbolic heart of Penn State, crowning the hill above the campus mall. The 1930 Georgian building sits on the site of the original 1859 College Building of the Farmers' High School and houses the Land-Grant Frescoes by Henry Varnum Poor. Grounds open daily; the lawn is the campus's ceremonial gathering place.

sights.address: Nittany Lion Shrine, Curtin Rd near Rec Hall, University Park, PA 16802
sights.w: One of the most photographed landmarks in Pennsylvania: a crouching mountain lion carved by sculptor Heinz Warneke from a 13-ton block of Indiana limestone, given by the Class of 1940. Reopened to visitors after a 2021-2022 site renovation; free, open-air, always accessible.

sights.n: Beaver Stadium & Penn State All-Sports Museum
sights.address: Beaver Stadium, 1 Beaver Stadium, University Park, PA 16802
sights.w: The 106,000-seat home of Penn State football and its All-Sports Museum, whose Upper and Lower galleries trace over a century of Nittany Lion athletics. Museum open Tue-Sat 10-4, Sun 12-4 (reduced winter hours; home-game-week changes); staff take guests to the club level for a view inside the bowl. Note: the stadium itself is under a multi-year renovation (Project Surge) through 2027.

sights.address: Palmer Museum of Art, The Arboretum at Penn State, Bigler Rd, University Park, PA 16802
sights.w: Penn State's art museum in a striking 73,000-sq-ft Allied Works building that opened June 1, 2024 at the edge of the Arboretum, nearly doubling exhibition space to 20 galleries with a store, cafe and sculpture path. Free admission; a genuine regional cultural destination.

sights.n: The Arboretum at Penn State (H.O. Smith Botanic Gardens)
sights.address: The Arboretum at Penn State, Bigler Rd & Park Ave, University Park, PA 16802
sights.w: 370 acres of gardens, meadows and woodland walks a mile west of Beaver Stadium, centered on the 10-acre H.O. Smith Botanic Gardens with pollinator habitats, water features, an Overlook Pavilion and a children's garden. Free admission, open dawn to dusk daily.

sights.address: 160 Curtin Rd, University Park, PA 16802
sights.w: A free insect museum across from the Berkey Creamery, reopened in 2022 after renovation, with a live arthropod zoo and a research collection of hundreds of thousands of specimens. Open to the public 10-4 Monday-Friday; admission free.

sights.address: Russell E. Larson Ag Research Center, 2710 W Pine Grove Rd, Pennsylvania Furnace, PA 16865
sights.w: A collection of some 3,000 tools and machines that fed, clothed and built rural Pennsylvania before electricity, at the Rock Springs research farm. Access is limited: open house days, group tours by appointment, and the free Ag Progress Days each August. Verify hours before visiting.

sights.address: College Ave & S Allen St, State College, PA 16801
sights.w: The historic pedestrian gateway between downtown and campus at the head of Allen Street, marking the original 1859 entrance to the College. The Class of 1916 Memorial Gateway frames the traditional gathering and celebration spot for the town. Free, open-air.

sights.address: 130 W College Ave, State College, PA 16801
sights.w: A 554-seat nonprofit community theatre built by Warner Bros. as a movie house in 1938 and restored as downtown's cultural hub for film, music and live performance. Active venue; check the calendar and box-office hours for shows.

sights.n: Downtown State College Public Art Walk (Calder Way murals)
sights.address: Calder Way, State College, PA 16801
sights.w: A self-guided downtown mural and public-art trail concentrated along Calder Way, including the community-painted Calder Way mural, MLK Plaza, and the 'Remember When' mural on the Dale Building at Fraser & Calder. Free walking tour mapped at StateCollegePublicArt.com; the scene peaks during the July Central Pennsylvania Festival of the Arts.

sights.address: High St & Allegheny St, Bellefonte, PA 16823
sights.w: A remarkably intact Victorian county-seat downtown along Spring Creek, listed on the National Register, built during a 19th-century iron-and-industry boom and once home to seven Pennsylvania governors. Grand houses, the 1889 railroad station and a walkable core of shops and eateries. Free, self-guided.

sights.address: Dunlap St, Bellefonte, PA 16823
sights.w: Bellefonte's 3.5-acre riverside park along Spring Creek, fed by the Big Spring that pours out 11+ million gallons a day and gave the town its name ("la belle fonte"). Riverwalk, the restored 1889 passenger station, gardens and an Underground Railroad history marker. Free, open daily.

sights.address: 160 Dunlap St, Bellefonte, PA 16823
sights.w: A National Register grist mill (1786/1894) on Spring Creek in Bellefonte's waterfront district, extensively restored and reopened in 2021 as a boutique hotel, restaurant and cocktail bar. A landmark on the Riverwalk; dine or stay to see the interior.

sights.address: 100 Match Factory Pl, Bellefonte, PA 16823
sights.w: The headquarters of the American Philatelic Society, the world's largest nonprofit stamp-collectors' organization, in the restored 1900 Pennsylvania Match Factory. Highlights include a fully reconstructed century-old general store and post office, a library and galleries. Open to visitors; check hours.

sights.n: Boalsburg Historic District (Birthplace of Memorial Day)
sights.address: Main St, Boalsburg, PA 16827
sights.w: A walkable stone-and-clapboard village that claims the first Memorial Day observance, traced to an 1864 cemetery gathering; the town center is full of shops, cafes and 18th-19th-century buildings and celebrates with a large Memorial Day weekend of events. Free, self-guided.

sights.address: 51 Boal Ave, Boalsburg, PA 16827
sights.w: Pennsylvania's museum of the citizen-soldier, set on the 28th Division Shrine grounds in Boalsburg. CLOSED to the public since Dec 8, 2024 for a $3.4M modernization (HVAC, geothermal, preservation systems); the reopening, once slated for Feb 2026, has slipped to 2027. The outdoor grounds and memorials remain worth a look; galleries are shut.

sights.address: 163 Boal Estate Dr, Boalsburg, PA 16827
sights.w: The estate of the Boal family since 1789, whose Columbus Chapel — brought from Spain in 1909 by a Columbus descendant who married into the family — holds the explorer's admiral's desk, two relics of the True Cross and centuries of European art. Guided 90-minute tours Wed-Sun at 2pm; other times by appointment.

sights.address: 1001 E College Ave, State College, PA 16801
sights.w: The restored ironmaster's mansion of Centre Furnace — the 18th-century iron works whose owners helped found Penn State — now the home of the Centre County Historical Society and listed on the National Register. Furnished to the Moses Thompson era (1842-1891). Guided tours on posted days; grounds and gardens open.

sights.address: Mount Nittany trailhead, 500 Mount Nittany Rd, Lemont, PA 16827
sights.w: The mountain that gives Happy Valley its identity, with 8 miles of trails and seven overlooks above the valley. The short climb to the Mike Lynch Overlook (marker #3, ~0.6 mi up) gives the classic view over State College and campus; the full loop is ~4.8 mi. Limited trailhead parking in Lemont; free.

sights.address: 222 Penns Cave Rd, Centre Hall, PA 16828
sights.w: America's only all-water cavern, toured entirely by boat, plus a wildlife park with a bus safari and off-road mountain tours. Cavern tours run Feb-Dec (daily 9-4 hourly in summer); the farm-nature-wildlife park runs Apr 1-Nov (closed for winter through Mar 31). Paid admission; the cave boat tour is not wheelchair accessible.

sights.address: 4216 Beaver Rd, Philipsburg, PA 16866
sights.w: A 3,394-acre park atop the Allegheny Plateau built around a 250-acre lake and one of the state's finest bogs (1,992-acre Natural Area) with orchids and carnivorous plants. The half-mile boardwalk Bog Trail is the signature walk; 20 miles of trails, swimming and boating. Free day use; open year-round.

sights.address: Rothrock State Forest, Bear Meadows Rd, Boalsburg, PA 16827
sights.w: A 96,000-acre forest of ridgelines, rhododendron valleys and mixed-oak woods wrapping the south side of the valley, prized for hiking, mountain biking and vistas (Bear Meadows Natural Area, the Mid State and Standing Stone trails). A multi-year purpose-built trail project is adding up to 47 miles; the first 7.5 opened in 2025. Free.

sights.address: Whipple Dam Rd, Petersburg, PA 16669
sights.w: A quiet 256-acre park in Rothrock State Forest around a 22-acre lake with a sand beach, swimming, non-powered boating and hiking, and a gateway to the surrounding 90,000 acres of forest. Free day use; open year-round.

sights.address: 15795 Greenwood Rd, Huntingdon, PA 16652
sights.w: A 406-acre park built around a restored 19th-century iron furnace and a six-acre lake, with a historic district, swimming beach, and 13.5 miles of trails that link into Rothrock and the Standing Stone/Mid State trails. Free day use; open year-round.

sights.address: 548 Puddintown Rd, State College, PA 16801
sights.w: A 62-acre nature center less than two miles from campus, pairing a historic farmstead with a 50-acre limestone-fed wetland crossed by a boardwalk. Run by Centre Region Parks & Recreation; grounds free and open daily, with programs and a visitor barn. Good for families and birders.

sights.address: 301 Bear Meadows Rd, Boalsburg, PA 16827
sights.w: The valley's four-season recreation hill: 14 ski/snowboard trails in winter and a summer Fun Centre with go-karts, mini-golf, batting cages, a skate park and driving range, plus an outdoor amphitheater for concerts. Paid activities; hours are seasonal.
